artifacts.summary: 5-phase implementation: durable gitignored deploy ledger library with hash + attributed-recency skip rules, checkpoint wiring, Group 11 end-to-end coverage incl. the named self-modifying acceptance criterion, runtime-file registration, and guardrails contract documentation.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a durable, gitignored, machine-local redeploy ledger (scripts/lib/deploy-ledger-lib.sh) with a content-hash skip and an attributed-recency skip to the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint, closing the repeated full-redeploy defect for both the ordinary cross-invocation case and the self-modifying-task class (deploy_pending override preserved as a backstop). Added 27 new unit tests and 7 new Group 11 end-to-end cases (including the named self-modifying-task acceptance criterion proving total deploy count stays 1 across 3 invocations), registered the ledger as an 18th gitignored runtime-file class member, and rewrote the guardrails contract documentation (Idempotence guard scope correction + new Durable redeploy ledger paragraph + D6 residual clause fix).

memory_candidates.content: When a task's own file_scope IS the source it redeploys/reverifies (a self-modifying-task class), a content-hash-based skip rule can never fire for it, because the task's own edits change the hash on every cycle by construction. Pair the hash rule with a second, attributed-recency rule: recent + shares an identity (task/session number) with the last successful run + every changed path is explained by that same run's own modified-files list. Shipping only the hash rule leaves the self-modifying class hitting the full (expensive) path on every single cycle.

check-extension-docs.sh (doc-lint) fails loudly when a new script file exists on disk under an extension's scripts/ tree but is absent from that extension's manifest.json provides.scripts array. Any task adding a new lib/ or tests/ script file under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/ must register it in manifest.json in the SAME change, or the next verify-deploy.sh run (fast gate, doc-lint check) fails even though the source code itself is correct.

A sourced bash library needing a fixed companion data file (e.g. a JSON reference file living at a known relative path beside the library) can resolve that path via its own BASH_SOURCE rather than requiring the caller to pass it as a function argument. This makes the library work identically whether it is sourced from the real deployed tree or copied into a test fixture that mirrors the same relative directory layout, with zero extra plumbing at call sites.
